methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: This study investigates the feasibility of implementing a solar-assisted adsorption chiller in an industrial building at the Oriental Weavers International factory

stage1.ineligibility_reason: Incidental EnPI/EnB mention. The paper is a techno-economic feasibility and optimization study of a solar-assisted adsorption chiller (TRNSYS simulation) replacing split-unit AC in an industrial building. Its 'energy performance indicators' are solar-fraction/thermal-power design metrics, and the energy 'baseline' is a pre-retrofit consumption estimate used for savings/CO2 comparison, not an EnPI/EnB measurement model normalising energy performance against relevant variables; no ISO 50001/50006 energy-management context is present.

paper_type.evidence_quote: The objective is to replace an inefficient split air conditioning system currently used

stage1.notes: Borderline eligibility (conf ~0.6). Paper has an explicit 'Energy performance indicators' section (solar fraction) and 'establishes a baseline' of existing-AC consumption (EER-degradation model), which broadly read could look like EnPI/EnB content. Called ineligible: these are solar-cooling design/feasibility metrics, not an ISO 50006 EnPI/EnB measurement model. Recommend human blind-first adjudication. level_3b=false regardless (not continuous-process).
